title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Ch. V 'Algèbre des figures'). F is a finite 'figure': a finite set of closed subsets (closed strata) of a space |F|, ordered by inclusion. Each A in F has an open stratum A°(F), and the open strata partition |F|. G ⊆ F is a sub-figure, and G ≤ F means G is saturated: if A ∈ F and |A| ⊂ |G| then A ∈ G. F' ≤ F is a subdivision with |F'| = |F|. It comes with the canonical map φ: F' → F, sending A' to the smallest element of F containing A'. F' induces on G a subdivision G' ≤ F' with |G'| = |G|.

The corollary of the previous page characterizes the subdivisions that change nothing outside G by equivalent conditions:
- b) φ restricts to a bijection F'∖G' → F∖G;
- c) for every A ∈ F∖G, A°(F) is an open stratum of F';
- d) F∖G ⊂ F';
- a) maximality among subdivisions of F inducing G' on G (crossed out, status hesitant).

This page finishes d) ⇒ b). Under d), φ is the identity on F∖G, so it remains to prove F∖G = F'∖G'.

1°) Take A ∈ F∖G and suppose A ∈ G'. Then |A| ⊂ |G'| = |G|. By saturation of G in F, A ∈ G, a contradiction.

2°) Take A' ∈ F'∖G'.
- Let A be the smallest element of F containing A', i.e. the minimum of the upper set F^{A'}. Then A' ⊂ A and A'°(F') ⊂ A°(F).
- A ∉ G. Otherwise A' ⊂ A ⊂ |G| = |G'|, and saturation of G' in F' would give A' ∈ G'.
- So A ∈ F∖G ⊂ F' by d).
- By a lemma proved later ('F' ≪ F'), A°(F) = A°(F').
- Hence two open strata of F' satisfy A'°(F') ⊂ A°(F'). Since open strata are disjoint, A = A' ∈ F.
- Finally A' ∉ G, by the same saturation argument.

The rough draft of b) ⇒ c) is crossed out and replaced by a cleaner proof of b) ⇔ c), completed on the next page. Set U = |F|∖|G| = |F'|∖|G'|, I* = F∖G and I'* = F'∖G'. These are open (upward-closed) subsets of the index posets I = F and I' = F'. The stratifications become surjections p: U → I* and p': U → I'*, with φ*: I'* → I* and p = φ*∘p'. The open strata are the fibres. b) says φ* is bijective; c) says every fibre of p is a fibre of p'. These are obviously equivalent.

The conceptual content is a dictionary: a stratification is a map from the space to its finite poset of strata, with open strata as fibres. Subdivision is factorization of such maps. 'Supported on G' means the factor map is bijective over the open complement.
errors: The final paragraph of 2°) (proving A' ∉ G) is redundant: A' = A has already been shown, and A ∉ G was proved just before.
Uses a forward-referenced lemma ('F' ≪ F', cf. lemme plus bas): an element of F that survives in F' keeps the same open stratum. It is not proved on this page.
The step A'°(F') ⊂ A°(F) silently uses that each open stratum of F' lies in a single open stratum of F, which is part of the definition of subdivision.
'(d'où A ∈ F)' should read 'd'où A' ∈ F'; A ∈ F holds by definition.

ideas.what: Finite stratification encoded by closed strata indexed by a poset, with open strata as fibres of a surjection U → I* onto an open (upward-closed) subset of the poset
ideas.modern_name: Poset-stratified space (map to a poset with the Alexandrov topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical in combinatorial topology; formalized for exit-path categories by MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (Higher Algebra, A.5)
ideas.where_published: The tame-topology programme is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this poset formulation is not there explicitly as far as I know

ideas.what: Saturated sub-figure G ≤ F (an element of F with support in |G| lies in G) and subdivisions F' ≤ F inducing G' on G
ideas.modern_name: Full subcomplex / closed union of strata; relative subdivision

ideas.what: Characterization of subdivisions supported on G: F∖G ⊂ F' ⇔ φ bijective F'∖G' → F∖G ⇔ open strata outside G remain open strata
ideas.modern_name: Subdivision that is trivial off a subcomplex (relative/minimal extension of a subdivision)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 'algebra of figures' systematically treats subdivisions of finite stratifications as factorizations of maps from the space to finite posets. This predates the exit-path/poset-stratified formalism of Treumann and Lurie. The content here is elementary, but it documents the foundations of his tame-topology programme.
missed.quote: les étoiles ouvertes de F qui sont ⊂ U ... sont les fibres de U →p I*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: shows concrete technical work toward the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse, in a language close to modern poset-stratified spaces. Not a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but elementary point-set/combinatorial lemma about relative subdivisions of stratifications. The poset-map viewpoint is mildly interesting historically, but the results are folklore.
transcription_corrections: Line 'donc A' ⊂ A°, A'°(F') ⊂ A°(F)': the first inclusion is more plausibly A' ⊂ A (the underlined passage).
Inserted phrase before 'F' ≪ F' reads roughly 'il s'agit de/il s'ensuit F' ≪ F' with 'cf lemme plus bas'; uncertain.
The left-margin vertical note (roughly 'je simplifie, cf plus bas'?) is not transcribed; reading uncertain.
'parties ouvertes [?]' is plausibly correct (open = upward-closed subsets of the index posets).
